quest.title: Vortex's Wake
quest.description: After your chance meeting with Zhongli, you learn that a Fatuus named Kliment is trying to organize an archaeological expedition. Zhongli is roped in as a consultant, along with an archaeologist named Wanyan who volunteers for the task. Though you distrust the Fatui, you join up at Zhongli's invitation. The first subject of this investigation is Osial, Overlord of the Vortex.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x500, Mora x27825, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

dialogues.speaker: Kliment
dialogues.text: This place looks so ordinary... Can we really find anything valuable here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Paimon thinks it looks really grand!

dialogues.speaker: Kliment
dialogues.text: I don't mean the scenery, but rather that there should be something out of the ordinary. A big battle did just occur and all... And I don't even know where to begin looking here.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Guyun Stone Forest is actually the perfect place to be if you wish to learn about the gods or the history of the Archon War.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Legend has it that Rex Lapis threw spears made of large rock into the sea here, piercing and crushing the Overlord of the Vortex.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: After many years of wind erosion, those stone spears have turned into the unique rock formations we see now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: These mountains were the Lord of Geo's weapons?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: What we see now is just the part of them that remains. The stone spears hurled by Rex Lapis, all those years ago, were much greater, both in number and in size.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: But due to the different angles they landed at, their large centers of mass, erosion by seawater, and years of gravity, many of them have been completely swallowed by the sea.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: So, besides wind erosion, the initial collapsing of the stone spears also played a big part in the formation of Guyun Stone Forest.

dialogues.speaker: Kliment
dialogues.text: Well... A god able to fight one so powerful as Rex Lapis was certainly very strong in its own right.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Indeed, this is where the value lies in research at Guyun Stone Forest.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Most of the objects from that time were lost to the sea, but the gigantic waves created by the Overlord of the Vortex have given those sunken objects a chance to see the light of day again.

dialogues.speaker: Kliment
dialogues.text: So you're saying that if we look carefully, we'll be able to get very, very rich—

dialogues.speaker: Kliment
dialogues.text: Uh, I mean — rich with archaeological knowledge and historical value, yes? That's all I seek in life.

dialogues.speaker: Kliment
dialogues.text: Well, since we brought so many people, I think it would be best to split up and look.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Okay then, I will go with my friend here. Although I have a smattering of knowledge in various disciplines, when it comes to archaeology, I can't compete with the expert here.

dialogues.speaker: Wanyan
dialogues.text: Huh? M—Me?

dialogues.speaker: Kliment
dialogues.text: What's the matter? This is your profession, why are you so surprised?

dialogues.speaker: Wanyan
dialogues.text: I get it... I'll escort him then.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Okay. If we find anything valuable or rare, let's meet on the shore opposite from here.

talks.objective: Use Elemental Sight to search for relics

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: The ancient god probably left behind lots of elemental marks. Following them should make our search much easier.

talks.objective: Defeat the opponents and open the chest
Continue using Elemental Sight to search for relics

Defeat the mimic monsters and recover the relic
Meet up with the other group

dialogues.speaker: Kliment
dialogues.text: ...You call yourself a scholar of archaeology? You can't even recognize this or that. What are you good for?

dialogues.speaker: Wanyan
dialogues.text: We all have our areas of expertise! I already tried very hard to explain!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Stop arguing! What in the world happened?

dialogues.speaker: Kliment
dialogues.text: This girl just keeps bragging about how she's an archaeologist, but she doesn't even know anything about the surrounding ruins! I even know more than her!

dialogues.speaker: Kliment
dialogues.text: She left me to rely solely on guessing — I mean, experience — to find anything valuable to take back. Ugh, what a waste of time!

dialogues.speaker: Wanyan
dialogues.text: I—I've just been researching the God of Salt, so I'm not familiar with sea relics. Is that so strange!?

response.speaker: Wanyan
response.text: And you! You kept asking about how much Mora everything is worth! Can the value of relics only be measured in Mora!?

response.speaker: Kliment
response.text: Uh... I mean, isn't measuring their value in Mora the easiest way? This also matches the traditions of Liyue, does it not?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Now, now, calm down, no need to make a fuss. We were able to bring back some intriguing objects. Let's have a look.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Oh...

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: What a shame. *sigh* These objects were indeed washed ashore by the Overlord of the Vortex, but they have nothing to do with the god besides being in the vicinity at the time.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: This stone slab we found, however, has a mysterious pattern and faint aura of divine power. Perhaps it will be useful for research purposes.

response.speaker: Kliment
response.text: Quick, give it to me!

response.speaker: Kliment
response.text: Hehe, at least we didn't come for nothing. The power of the gods, yes! This is good... heh.

response.speaker: Kliment
response.text: Oh, but these other objects are certainly worth a little something, right? It should be enough to cover the cost of hiring you — it's all mine!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So... it's only valuable for research if there are remnants of divine power on it?

response.speaker: Wanyan
response.text: Not at all. My quest to uncover the history of the God of Salt is because history can tell us about culture and beliefs...

response.speaker: Wanyan
response.text: But YOU... You're just trying to use archaeology to get rich!

response.speaker: Kliment
response.text: Nonsense! I'm a professional archaeology researcher from Snezhnaya, I swear. If I'm lying, may the Lord of Geo strike me down!

choices.text: (No, you're trying to get rich off archaeology...)

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Oh, by the way. You probably don't want to sell that teacup.

response.speaker: Kliment
response.text: Oh, why's that?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: That's not an ancient teacup. It's part of Ningguang's collection, it must have fallen here along with the Jade Chamber. So unless you want to mess with the Qixing...

response.speaker: Kliment
response.text: Ah, I see... What a shame. It was of such high quality, too.

response.speaker: Wanyan
response.text: See!? You do want to sell these objects!

response.speaker: Kliment
response.text: S—So what! Why can't I pursue wealth both intellectual and material? Don't be so simple-minded!

response.speaker: Kliment
response.text: Alright then! No need to stay here any longer. Hm, I'm rather quite intrigued by the God of Salt too, actually. Let's go to Sal Terrae next.

choices.text: (No, you're trying to collect the strength of the gods...)
(One shouldn't lack general knowledge in their field...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Well, go ahead then, {NICKNAME}. Use your Elemental Sight to look for any marks.
